newsitem.title: DUBAI: Zhirinovsky says U.S. offered him money to quit.
newsitem.headline: Zhirinovsky says U.S. offered him money to quit.

text.p: Russian ultranationalist Vladimir Zhirinovsky was on Thursday quoted as saying the United States had offered him $100 million in 1994 to quit politics.

Zhirinovsky, who has described U.S. President Bill Clinton as "worse than Hitler" for launching air strikes against Iraq, made his comments in an interview with al-Khaleej newspaper of the United Arab Emirates.
"...In January 1994 after I was elected to parliament in December 1993 they offered me $100 million in return for me to quit politics, my party and my country," he said.

"They sent an envoy from the United States and offered me the money a month after my election and when I said that that was impossible (accepting the money) they started fighting me every day and every hour...to make me look bad."
